d:
Indr chalisa is a chant for courage, to one of the oldest gods of Hinduism.
Indra is the most invoked deity in the Rigveda. Roughly a quarter of its 1,028 hymns call his name, more than Agni, more than Vishnu, more than anyone. He breaks the serpent that dams the rivers, splits the cave that hides the light, and rides into battle beside mortal kings as a friend, not a master. And then, somewhere across three thousand years, we stopped singing to him. Nearly every major deity today has a Chalisa. Indra has none. No living devotional tradition, no forty verses, nothing to chant.
